summary: Kunio Mugitani works in sinology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied under Mitsuji Fukunaga around 1970–1977 and served as a professor at Kyoto University from around 1992 to 2012.
Kunio Odaka studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1928 to 1931. He later held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1947–1969) and Sophia University (~1969–1979).

Kunio Yanagita worked in religious studies and Japanology after studying law at the University of Tokyo (~1897–1900). He held posts at the Ministry of Agriculture and Commerce, Tokyo Asahi Shimbun, Privy Council, and Kokugakuin University (~1949–1960).

Philosopher Kuno Fischer studied at Leipzig University (~1844–1845) and the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1845–1847). He served on the faculties of the University of Jena (~1856–1872) and Heidelberg University (~1872–1907).

Philosopher Kuno Lorenz completed his PhD at Kiel University (1961) and his Habilitation at Erlangen-Nuremberg (1969). He held a chair in philosophy at the University of Hamburg (1970) and was a professor at Saarland University (1974–1998).
Linguist Kuno Meyer studied at Leipzig University under Ernst Windisch (~1879–1884). He held posts at the University of Liverpool (~1884–1911) and Frederick William University Berlin (~1911–1919).

Working in philosophy and Buddhist studies, Kuntala Bhattacharya earned her PhD at Jadavpur University under Amita Chatterjee and Shyamapada Misra (attested 2009). She held a post at Rabindra Bharati University (attested 2009).
Kunzang Namgyal studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and taught Tertön Sogyal.
Kunzang Pelden studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Patrul Rinpoche. He taught Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, and Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen.

id: P:Kunzig Shamar Rinpoche Mipham Chokyi Lodro
summary: Active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Kunzig Shamar Rinpoche Mipham Chokyi Lodro studied under traditional teachers Rangjung Rigpe Dorje and Kalu Rinpoche (1973).
Working in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology, Kurt A. Behrendt earned his PhD from UCLA in 1997. Around 2006, he served as assistant curator of Asian art at the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
Kurt Andrew Johnson, a scholar of Indology and history and archaeology, completed his PhD at the University of York in 2010 under the supervision of Jane Moody.
Philosopher Kurt Huber earned his PhD at the University of Munich (~1913–1917). He remained there for his academic career, serving as extraordinary professor in 1926 and full professor in 1938.

Kurt Tropper works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a doctoral degree from the University of Vienna (2001) under Ernst Steinkellner, and held posts at the University of Vienna and the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

A scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Kurtis R. Schaeffer earned an MA at the University of Washington and a PhD at Harvard (~1995–2000). He held posts at the University of Alabama (2000–2004) and the University of Virginia (2005).
Kurunegoda Piyatissa worked in Buddhist studies and served as head of the New York Buddhist Vihara (attested 1998, 2009).

Working in Buddhist and religious studies, Kwangsoo Park earned an MA from the University of Iowa and a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison. He served as a professor at Wonkwang University (attested 2020).
Active in Sinology and Indology, Kwei-Sun Wei completed a PhD at Aligarh Muslim University and served as a professor at Visva-Bharati University.

Kyo Kano studied Indology and philosophy at Keio, Kyoto, and Vienna universities. Kano served as an assistant at Kyoto University (attested 1989) and as an associate professor at Kobe Women's University (attested 2000).

Kyojun Shimizudani studied at Tendai Sect University and Taisho University. He served as professor at Tendai Sect University (1919) and Taisho University (1926–1945), and was chief abbot (kanju) of Sensō-ji from around 1952 to 1979.
